docs.title: Grumpy Jr – Getting Started
docs.text: Follow these instructions to install the batteries and configure your Grumpy Jr repeater using the MeshCore Companion app.

docs.title: Step 1 – Prepare Your MeshCore Companion
docs.text: Before beginning, make sure your MeshCore Companion is powered on and synced with your phone.

docs.title: Step 2 – Remove the Rear Panel
docs.text: Using the provided T20 wrench, remove the T20 bolts securing the rear panel of the repeater. Carefully remove the back plate.

docs.title: Step 3 – Install the Batteries
docs.text: Insert both 21700 lithium batteries into the battery compartment, making sure they are properly seated.

docs.title: Step 4 – Locate Your Grumpy Mesh Repeater
docs.text:
Watch the Contacts list in your MeshCore app for a repeater named:

Grumpymesh Repeater XXXX

The XXXX represents your order number.

Note: If you ordered more than one repeater, each repeater will use the same order number followed by a sequential letter (A, B, C, D, etc.) to identify each individual unit.

docs.title: Step 5 – Connect to Your Grumpy Mesh Repeater
docs.text:
Once you see your repeater in the Contacts list, select its name.

When prompted for a password, enter:

  • Admin Password: Admin
  • Guest Password: hello

Keep the Guest password handy for future use.

docs.title: Step 6 – Rename Your Repeater
docs.text: Once connected, navigate to Settings in the MeshCore app. Find the repeater name setting and rename it to whatever name you prefer.

docs.title: Step 7 – Confirm Your Repeater Radio Settings
docs.text:
Verify that your repeater's radio settings are correct for your area.

If you provided a location during your order and the appropriate regional settings could be identified, your repeater should already be configured.

The preset will be labeled either US or Canada. Both presets use the same settings.

  • Default: SF 7 / CR 5
  • Extended range: SF 7 / CR 8

Range tip: If your repeater is far from other repeaters, use CR 8 for the best range.

docs.title: Step 8 – Set Advert Intervals
docs.text:
Confirm the advert intervals for your region.

Current defaults:

  • Local: 240 minutes
  • Flood: 23 hours

Change these settings to match your local mesh group's recommendations.

docs.title: Step 9 – Set Your Repeater Location
docs.text:
In the Location section, enter the location where your repeater is installed. You can also use the map icon to choose an approximate location.

Privacy tip: If you do not want to show the exact location of your repeater, it is okay to choose a place one or two blocks away.

docs.title: Step 10 – Save Your Repeater Settings
docs.text: Once you have confirmed your repeater name, radio settings, advert intervals, and location, press Save to apply your changes.

docs.title: Step 11 – Manage Regional Codes (If Applicable)
docs.text:
If your region has started using MeshCore Region Codes, open Manage Regions.

Here you can confirm any region codes that may already have been entered and add any additional region codes used in your area.

When finished:

  1. Press the check mark at the top of the screen.
  2. Press Reboot to restart your repeater and apply the changes.

docs.title: Step 12 – You're Ready to Go!
docs.text: Congratulations! Your Grumpy Jr repeater is now configured and ready for use.

docs.title: Alternative Setup Using USB-C
docs.text:
If your repeater does not advertise its name or appear in your MeshCore app's Contacts list, you can configure it using the USB-C port located on the bottom of the repeater.

  1. Connect the repeater to your computer using the USB-C port.
  2. Visit the MeshCore Flasher website.
  3. Open the Repeater Setup program.
  4. Select your repeater and configure it using the same options outlined above, including your repeater name, location, radio settings, advert intervals, and regional codes.
  5. Save your settings and reboot the repeater.

docs.title: Update Firmware Over Wi-Fi
docs.text: Follow these steps to upgrade your Grumpy Jr repeater firmware over Wi-Fi.

docs.title: Step 1 – Download the Firmware
docs.text:
On the device you will use to update the repeater:

  1. Go to the MeshCore website.
  2. Select Flasher.
  3. Select Heltec V4.
  4. Select Repeater.
  5. Choose Download.
  6. Do not download the Merged version. Download the other version instead.
  7. Remember where you saved the firmware file. You will need it later during the OTA update.

docs.title: Step 2 – Remotely Access Your Repeater
docs.text: Using your phone and MeshCore Companion app, remotely access your Grumpy Jr repeater.

docs.title: Step 3 – Log In as Administrator
docs.text: When prompted, enter your Admin password to access the repeater's administrative settings.

docs.title: Step 4 – Open the Command Line
docs.text: Press the Command Line button located in the middle of the bottom of the screen.

docs.title: Step 5 – Start the OTA Update
docs.text:
In the Send a Command section, type the following command exactly as shown, using all lowercase letters:

start ota

docs.title: Step 6 – Confirm OTA Mode Has Started
docs.text:
After sending the start ota command, the repeater should respond with:

Started: https://192.168.4.1/update

  • If you do not see this response: Repeat Step 5.
  • If you see this response: Proceed to Step 7.

docs.title: Step 7 – Connect to the MeshCore OTA Wi-Fi Network
docs.text:
Open the Wi-Fi SSID list on your phone and look for:

Meshcore-OTA

Select this network to connect.

  • There is no password required.
  • Give your phone a few seconds to connect.
  • You should see Meshcore-OTA displayed as connected in your Wi-Fi settings.

docs.title: Step 8 – Open the OTA Update Page
docs.text:
Open the web browser on your phone or device and enter:

https://192.168.4.1/update

docs.title: Step 9 – Upload the Firmware
docs.text:
An OTA upload page should open, prompting you to upload the firmware you want to install.

  1. Press Choose File.
  2. Browse to the folder where you saved your firmware.
  3. Select the firmware file you wish to upload.
  4. The repeater will automatically begin uploading the firmware.
  5. Watch the progress bar as it advances to 100%.

Once the upload reaches 100%, the repeater will automatically reboot to complete the firmware upgrade.

docs.title: Step 10 – Verify Your Firmware Version
docs.text:
Go back into your repeater settings in the MeshCore app.

Select Version at the bottom of the screen and confirm that your Grumpy Jr is running the new firmware version.

Enjoy your upgraded Grumpy Jr repeater!

docs.title: Important Note – Reboot If You Cannot Connect to Meshcore-OTA
docs.text:
If you are too far away from your repeater to connect to the Meshcore-OTA Wi-Fi network and several attempts are unsuccessful, you must remotely connect back to your repeater through the MeshCore Companion app and reboot the repeater.

If you do not reboot it, the repeater's Wi-Fi will remain enabled and continue draining the batteries until they die.

Battery warning: The Heltec V4 is known to sometimes become unresponsive after its batteries have completely discharged, even after solar charging is restored. Avoid allowing the batteries to drain completely.

docs.title: The Grumpy Mesh Board
docs.text:
STANDALONE MESHCORE HARDWARE

The Grumpy Mesh Board is a dummy product page for a compact, high-output MeshCore board. It is intended to become the home for final specifications, assembly notes, and ordering information.

1WMeshCore radio SMAAntenna connector Wi-FiExternal antenna OTAFirmware updates

docs.title: Built by the community
docs.text: This board was built by the Gulf Coast Mesh community, on what has been learned on from over 300 repeater deployments.

docs.title: Power management
docs.text:
The board accepts a 5v input for power, either via USB or the 5v power connector. When you purchuse a Grumpy Mesh Board, you'll recieve a waveshare solar controller, and all the cables needed to connect it to the board.

Once connected, The board will be able to not only be powered via a battery with solar. But also be able to monitor the voltage of the battery, unlike every other repeater out there that uses a external solar board.

The advantages of this, is a robust, and reliable repeater. The board can fully drain out it's battiers in the rare event of no sun for days, and still auto recover when sun comes back.

docs.title: Wi-Fi and OTA updates
docs.text: The board also includes an external antenna for your board, but it also allows you to add any wifi antenna with a ipex connector; For long range over the air updates.

docs.title: Expansion port
docs.text:
The board includes a Expansion port, This allowing you to add additional accessories like temperature sensors to monitor your enclosure or outside temperature, a wind sensor, rain sensor, and almost anything you'd like. With open documentation on how to use it, the possibilities are endless.

Move To Getting Started Guide

docs.title: What is the purpose of the expansion port on the Grumpy Board?
docs.text: The expansion port on the Grumpy Board allows for additional functionality and sensors. It provides a simple way to connect sensors, like the tempture sensor's, wind sensor, rain sensor. Along with more advice features like Celluar modem's.

docs.title: How does the expansion port work?
docs.text: Below is a diagram of the Expansion Port on the Grumpy Board, It's a 4 pin JST-PH connected that prodives 3.3v and 5v power along with 1 data pin for I2C communication.

docs.title: How do I interact with the expansion port?
docs.text:
The Grumpy Board has firmware built avilable via the flasher for a standard i2c tempture sensor, the firmware for the Grumpy board is open source and welcome to have additonal sensor support added.

You can also make a Github issue on this repository if you would like for us to help you intergrate your sensor or device.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Do not power on the board without an antenna attached. Doing so may damage the board and void exchanges.

docs.title: Thank you for buying a Grumpy Board
This guide will explain how to assemble and set up your Grumpyboard from start to finish.
docs.text:
Each board purchased comes with the following:

  • 1x GrumpyBoard
  • 1x Waveshare Solar Board
  • 2x JST-PH Power Leads
  • 1x Wi-Fi antenna
  • 1x Quality Control Card
  • 1x Getting Started Guide (which brought you here)

docs.title: How to assemble your board
docs.text:
To get started assembling your board, you'll need the following:

  • A Phillips screwdriver
  • A small flathead screwdriver
  • Unbox your board: Remove your board from its bag, along with the solar board and the included parts.
  • Remove the standoffs: Included with your Waveshare are 4x standoffs. We will be swapping these for the longer standoffs included in the bag. Use your Phillips screwdriver to remove all 4x screws (save these; you will be using them later).
  • Attach your standoffs: Inside your bag, there will be 4x 10mm 2.5mm standoffs. Using the screws that came with the Waveshare, attach each standoff to the Waveshare solar board.
  • Install the Waveshare on your Grumpy Board: Using the 4x 6mm 2.5mm screws included in the bag, place the Waveshare on the Grumpy Board with the USB-C port facing the right side of the Grumpy Board. Loosely install 2 screws to align the standoffs correctly, then insert the other 2 screws diagonally and tighten all 4.
  • Wire your battery: Using your flathead screwdriver, loosen the 2x wire terminals on the bottom of the solar board. Attach one of the JST-PH Power Leads included in your order to the left battery port on your Grumpy Board. Take the red wire from the lead and connect it to the left wire terminal on the right port labeled "+" on the board. Connect the black wire to the right wire terminal on the left port labeled "-". You can now wire your battery into this port, connecting the negative wire to "-" and the positive wire to "+".
  • Wire your 5V power source: On the other side, repeat the same process. Plug the other included JST-PH lead into the right 5V power input port. Connect the red wire from this lead to the left wire terminal on the right port labeled "+", and connect the black wire to the right wire terminal on the left port labeled "-". You can now wire your 5V power source into this port, connecting the negative wire to "-" and the positive wire to "+".
  • Tighten everything, and you're done! Inspect the wires and make sure they are all connected to the correct ports. Tighten the 4x wire terminal screws and visually inspect the entire board. You now have a finished and assembled Grumpy Board.

docs.title: How to flash your board
docs.text:
To get started flashing your board, you'll need the following:

  • A computer running Linux, Windows, or macOS.
  • A USB-C cable that can handle data and power.
  • An SMA or IPEX antenna in the 915 MHz range.
  • Connect the antenna: Insert the included IPEX Wi-Fi antenna into the ESP32 connector positioned near the USB-C port.
  • Attach your antenna: Connect your SMA or IPEX antenna to the board using either the SMA mount on top or the IPEX port beneath it.
  • Connect via USB-C: Plug a USB-C cable into the GrumpyBoard and connect the other end to your computer.
  • Put the board into boot mode: Hold down the left button on the Grumpy Board, then press the right button once. Release the left button, and your board will now be in boot mode.
  • Visit the flashing portal: Navigate to Grumpymesh.com/flasher in your web browser.
  • Choose firmware: Select the firmware type you prefer: Client or Repeater.
  • Select whether you'd like Wi-Fi configuration: If you choose Repeater, you will be asked whether you'd like to configure the board via a Wi-Fi web portal. If you choose to enable it, the board will create a Wi-Fi access point called "Grumpymesh" after it reboots for the first time. You can then use this portal to configure the board's settings via a phone or computer.
  • Flash the firmware: Click Erase and then click the Flash button. Your browser will ask you to select the device at the top left.
  • Wait 1–2 minutes: After the flashing process is complete, you will have a flashed GrumpyBoard ready to use.

docs.title: Via USB
docs.text:
• Plug in via USB-C: Plug a USB-C cable into the GrumpyBoard and connect the other end to your computer.
  • Open the web configurator: Navigate to Grumpymesh.com/flasher in your browser. Click "Repeater setup" on the left side.
  • Click Connect: At the top right, click Connect, then select the Grumpy Board at the top left.
  • Program: Follow each section and enter the required information.
  • Click Save: Click Save at the bottom right.
